corpus_definition: To move to the next side of a sheet of paper.
particle_note: Here used without an object: "Please turn over." With an object it is separable: "turn the page over / turn over the page"; with a pronoun only "turn it over".

relations.note: Turn something so the other side is on top; informal.

context.text: The teacher said, "Do not turn over the test paper yet." When she said "Go," we all turned the papers over.

corpus_definition: Make the sound of a device louder.
particle_note: Separable: "turn up the music / turn the music up"; with a pronoun only "turn it up".

relations.note: More formal: make the level higher.
Make the sound or heat lower.

context.text: My brother loves this song, so he turned up the radio. Mum was cooking and asked him to turn it up even more.

reviewer_note: "turn up" = arrive is a different meaning, not covered.

corpus_definition: To write using a keyboard on a computer.

forms.definition: the work or skill of writing with a keyboard
forms.example: My typing is fast because I practise every day.

forms.definition: a kind or sort of person or thing
forms.example: What type of music do you like?
forms.note: Belongs to type = kind, not writing on a keyboard.

forms.definition: to write words on a computer by pressing keys
forms.example: Please type your name at the top.

syn.note: Put words or numbers into a computer.
General word; type means using keys.

forms.definition: written with a keyboard, not by hand
forms.example: Send a typed copy of your letter.

ant.note: Written by hand with a pen.

people.definition: a person whose job is writing documents on a keyboard
people.example: The office needs a new typist.

context.text: Jasur types his homework on his laptop. His typing is very fast because he plays computer games.

reviewer_note: type (kind) is a different meaning. typewriter is a compound, left out.

corpus_definition: Not having the skill or chance to do something.

forms.definition: the fact of not being able to do something
forms.example: His inability to swim worried his mother.

forms.definition: to hurt someone so a part of their body does not work, or to stop a machine working
forms.example: You can disable the alarm with this button.
forms.note: Belongs to able = having a working body, not chance or skill here.

forms.definition: not having the skill, time or chance to do something
forms.example: I was unable to find my keys.
forms.note: Always followed by to + verb: "unable to come".

syn.note: Same meaning; more common in speech.
More formal; not having the ability.

ant.note: Having the skill or chance to do something.

context.text: Malika was unable to come to the party because she was ill. Her inability to go out made her sad all weekend.

reviewer_note: Used only as "unable to + verb", never before a noun.

usage_note: Preposition ("underneath the bed") or adverb ("a shirt with a T-shirt underneath"). A little more informal and stronger than "under": often means hidden or covered.

relations.note: Lower than something, not always touching or covered.
Resting on the highest part of something.

context.text: Dilnoza hid the present underneath her bed. Underneath the bed there was also an old box of photos.

reviewer_note: Function word; covered vs under noted.

corpus_definition: To give the latest information or change to a newer version.

forms.definition: the newest information, or a newer version of software
forms.example: There is a new update for this app.

syn.note: A better version, often one you pay for.

forms.definition: to make something newer or give someone the latest news

syn.note: Change to a better version.
Make something more modern; British English also modernise.
Load the newest version of a page.

forms.definition: changed so that it is new and correct
forms.example: Here is the updated list of students.

syn.note: Happening or true now.

ant.note: Old and not used any more.

context.text: My phone asked me to update the apps last night. The updated maps app now shows the new metro stations in Tashkent.

reviewer_note: Noun and verb share spelling; updated as participial adjective.

corpus_definition: To move digital content from your device to the web.

forms.definition: a file that you send from your device to the internet

ant.note: A file you get from the internet onto your device.

forms.definition: to send files from your computer or phone to the internet
forms.example: You can upload your photos to the website.

syn.note: Put a message or photo on social media.
Put something online for other people to see.

ant.note: Get a file from the internet onto your device.

context.text: Sevara uploads videos of her cooking every Friday. Each upload gets many likes from her friends.

reviewer_note: Only one spelling in the family; download in ant.

corpus_definition: Something that helps you do a job or task effectively.

forms.definition: the act of using something, or the purpose it has
forms.example: This tool has many uses in the kitchen.

forms.definition: the quality of helping you do something
forms.example: Nobody doubts the usefulness of a good dictionary.

forms.definition: to do something with a thing for a purpose

syn.note: Formal: use a method or skill.
Use a rule or method in a situation.

forms.definition: helping you to do or get what you want
forms.example: This map is very useful for tourists.

syn.note: Same meaning; also used about people.
Informal: useful and easy to use.
Good for real, everyday use.

forms.definition: in a way that helps or is useful
forms.example: You can spend your free time usefully.

people.definition: a person who uses a machine, service or product
people.example: The app has a million users.

context.text: This dictionary app is very useful for my English lessons. I use it every day on the bus to school.

reviewer_note: useless placed in ant; user in People & things.

corpus_definition: a card or gift given to someone you love on February 14th

forms.definition: a card or present you give to someone you love on 14 February
forms.example: He sent her a valentine with a short poem.
forms.note: Also the person you send it to: "Will you be my valentine?"

syn.note: A letter that says you love someone.

context.text: On 14 February Sardor gave Madina a valentine. Inside the valentine he wrote a short poem.

reviewer_note: Valentine's Day is the holiday name; only one family form.

corpus_definition: A vehicle used for carrying goods or a large group.

forms.definition: a vehicle bigger than a car, used for carrying things or people
forms.example: They put all the boxes into the van.

syn.note: British English: a much bigger vehicle for goods.
American English for a big goods vehicle.
A small bus for about ten to twenty people.

context.text: When we moved house, my uncle came with his van. We put the sofa and all our boxes into it.
